question: How many confirmed measles cases will Wisconsin DHS report for 2026 as of November 27, 2026?

calls.reasoning: 651 confirmed as of Nov 13 (DHS page). Weekly additions doubled from ~85 to 174 in the week to Nov 13; Grant County went from 153 to 222 in 3 days. Resolution uses either the Nov 24 or the Nov 27 (post-Thanksgiving, possibly delayed) update. Holding 174/wk steady gives ~925-1000; continued acceleration gives 1100-1300; burnout/vaccination slowing gives ~820-860. The Nov 13 jump may include a reporting backlog. Market check: no Wisconsin-specific market on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold; only national CDC-count contracts, which don't match.

- Increments: +46 (Nov 3-6, 3d), +74 (Nov 6-10, 4d), +100 (Nov 10-13, 3d). Weekly: ~85 (Oct 30-Nov 6), 174 (Nov 6-13; media: most of any state that week).

- Wastewater detections in Iowa, Grant, Lafayette and Green counties (DHS page). 99.4% of cases unvaccinated. About 2,000 MMR doses delivered since Aug 1; early infant MMR authorized.
- A Nov 13 jump could partly be a reporting backlog (unverified).

- Resolves off the DHS outbreaks-page headline N, not county figures, not CDC.
- Event window: value is a snapshot at 2026-11-27 23:59 UTC; as of Nov 17 the latest data is 14 days before the latest possible data date (Nov 27) or 11 days before Nov 24.
- Scenario anchors (arithmetic, not forecasts): 174/wk constant gives ~925 on Nov 24 and ~1000 on Nov 27; 100/wk gives ~810/~850; 260-390/wk gives ~1080/~1300.
- Markets: none Wisconsin-specific; Polymarket/Kalshi have only national CDC-count thresholds.
- Searched but not found: Nov 17 DHS update, epi curve by rash-onset week, DHS statement on Thanksgiving posting schedule.
calls.reference_class: Linear/exponential extrapolation of US close-knit-community measles outbreaks (e.g. West Texas 2025) in their growth phase, 2-week horizon

calls.reasoning: Headline stood at 651 as of Nov 13. Increments per update have been rising: about 10, 15, 18 and then 33 cases/day between Oct 30 and Nov 13, so weekly additions roughly doubled. The deciding figure will most likely be the Nov 24 update (11 days after Nov 13), or the Nov 27 update if it posts before the deadline. The reference class is large measles outbreaks in close-knit undervaccinated communities (TX 2025, SC 2025-26). These tend to rise for weeks, hit a peak, and then slow once reactive vaccination takes hold. Holding the recent ~25-33/day gives about 930-1110. Slowing to ~15/day gives about 820-860, and continued acceleration gives 1150-1300. Holiday reporting delays push the number down. No human prediction market was found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.

calls.reconciliation: All three dossiers agree on the facts: 651 as of Nov 13, the headline series, the Tue/Fri cadence, and that resolution most likely comes from the Nov 24 or Nov 27 update. No factual disputes needed settling. The runs differ only in judgment about the growth rate (23/day for Run 3 versus 25-33/day for Runs 1-2) and in how much weight to give holiday delays. I take a ~25/day path, judging that the slowing forces (saturation, vaccination, a possible backlog in the Nov 13 figure) roughly offset the spread to new counties. That gives a median of 950. I keep the runs' dispersion of about 400, which I agree with. No market was found by the harness or the runs; I retrieved nothing myself.
